stem: Containers are draining into trays that retain standing water around their bases after irrigation. What is the strongest corrective action?
choices: Increase irrigation volume so the trays overflow more often, using the extra drainage to move stagnant water away from the containers
Restore free drainage and prevent prolonged contact with standing water before changing the nutrient recipe or other unrelated settings
Raise fertilizer EC to offset the diluted root zone, because standing water mainly lowers nutrient concentration around the roots
Keep the irrigation program unchanged while canopy color remains normal, because tray water affects roots only after visible symptoms appear
rationale: Standing drainage water can interfere with normal drainage and keep the lower root zone excessively wet. Restoring free drainage addresses the root-zone physical condition before unrelated nutrient changes are made.
